newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine to sell stakes in two regional power firms.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine to sell stakes in two regional power firms.

text.p: Ukraine's State Property Fund (FDM) plans to hold tenders before July for stakes in two large regional power companies, a fund spokesman said at the weekend.
Foreign investors will be able to participate in investment tenders for 26.45 percent of Kirovohradoblenergo and 24.38 percent of Cherkassyoblenergo.
The winner of an investment tender is the bidder offering the most investment in the company, not the highest price for the stake.
The Ministry of Energy and Electrification will keep 51 percent of both companies.
The authorised capital of Kirovohradoblenergo, which serves Ukraine's central Kirovohrad region, is 29.8 million hryvnias, or 2,984,400 shares with a face value of 10 hryvnias each.
Its pre-tax profit was 4.4 million hryvnias in 1996. No figures were available for 1995.
Outstanding debts at the end of last year totalled 28.2 million hryvnias, and the company is owed 25.5 million hryvnias.
The company employs 3,000 workers, who along with managers are entitled to a 22.55 percent share of the power company.
The authorised capital of Cherkassyoblenergo, serving the Cherkassy region 200 kilometres south of Kiev, is 37 million hryvnias, or 148,393,332 shares with a face value of 00.25 hryvnias each.
Its 1996 pre-tax profit was 1.61 million hryvnias. Outstanding debts at the end of last year were 28.5 million hryvnias and the company is owed 28.8 million hryvnias.
Cherkassyoblenergo employs 4,900 workers, who together with managers are entitled to a 24.62 percent stake.
The plan to privatise all 18 of Ukraine's regional power companies was approved by the government last month.
